verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 46.6
verses.english: Linked Discourses 46.6

verses.pali: 1. Pabbatavagga
verses.english: 1. Mountains

verses.pali: Kuṇḍaliyasutta
verses.english: Kuṇḍaliya

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sākete viharati añjanavane migadāye.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāketa in the deer park at the Añjana Wood.

verses.pali: Atha kho kuṇḍaliyo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the wanderer Kuṇḍaliya went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho kuṇḍaliyo paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “ahamasmi, bho gotama, ārāmanissayī parisāvacaro.
verses.english: “Worthy Gotama, I like to hang around the monasteries and visit the assemblies.

verses.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, bho gotama, pacchābhattaṁ bhuttapātarāsassa ayamācāro hoti—
verses.english: When I’ve finished breakfast, it’s my habit to

verses.pali: ārāmena ārāmaṁ uyyānena uyyānaṁ anucaṅkamāmi anuvicarāmi.
verses.english: wander from monastery to monastery, from park to park.

verses.pali: So tattha passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe itivādappamokkhānisaṁsañceva kathaṁ kathente upārambhānisaṁsañca:
verses.english: There I see some ascetics and brahmins speaking for the sake of winning debates and finding fault.

verses.pali: ‘bhavaṁ pana gotamo kimānisaṁso viharatī’”ti?
verses.english: But what benefit does the worthy Gotama live for?”

verses.pali: “Vijjāvimuttiphalānisaṁso kho, kuṇḍaliya, tathāgato viharatī”ti.
verses.english: “The benefit the Realized One lives for, Kuṇḍaliya, is the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

verses.pali: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrentī”ti?
verses.english: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill knowledge and freedom?”

verses.pali: “Satta kho, kuṇḍaliya, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrentī”ti.
verses.english: “The seven awakening factors.”

verses.pali: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī”ti?
verses.english: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill the seven awakening factors?”

verses.pali: “Cattāro kho, kuṇḍaliya, satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī”ti.
verses.english: “The four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”

verses.pali: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā, bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrentī”ti?
verses.english: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation?”

verses.pali: “Tīṇi kho, kuṇḍaliya, sucaritāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrentī”ti.
verses.english: “The three kinds of good conduct.”

verses.pali: “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrentī”ti?
verses.english: “But what things must be developed and cultivated in order to fulfill the three kinds of good conduct?”

verses.pali: “Indriyasaṁvaro kho, kuṇḍaliya, bhāvito bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūretīti.
verses.english: “Sense restraint.

verses.pali: Kathaṁ bhāvito ca, kuṇḍaliya, indriyasaṁvaro kathaṁ bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūretīti?
verses.english: And Kuṇḍaliya, how is sense restraint developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the three kinds of good conduct?

verses.pali: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā manāpaṁ nābhijjhati nābhihaṁsati, na rāgaṁ janeti.
verses.english: A mendicant sees an agreeable sight with their eye. They don’t desire it or enjoy it, and they don’t give rise to greed.

verses.pali: Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ajjhattaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ.
verses.english: Their mind and body are steady internally, well settled and well freed.

verses.pali: Cakkhunā kho paneva rūpaṁ disvā amanāpaṁ na maṅku hoti appatiṭṭhitacitto adīnamānaso abyāpannacetaso.
verses.english: But if they see a disagreeable sight they’re undismayed, with mind unirritated, spirit undaunted, and heart unangered.

verses.pali: Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ajjhattaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ.
verses.english: Their mind and body are steady internally, well settled and well freed.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu sotena saddaṁ sutvā …pe…
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant hears an agreeable sound with the ear …

verses.pali: ghānena gandhaṁ ghāyitvā …pe…
verses.english: smells an agreeable odor with the nose …

verses.pali: jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā …pe…
verses.english: tastes an agreeable flavor with the tongue …

verses.pali: kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṁ phusitvā …pe…
verses.english: feels an agreeable touch with the body …

verses.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya manāpaṁ nābhijjhati nābhihaṁsati, na rāgaṁ janeti.
verses.english: knows an agreeable idea with their mind. They don’t desire it or enjoy it, and they don’t give rise to greed.

verses.pali: Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ajjhattaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ.
verses.english: Their mind and body are steady internally, well settled and well freed.

verses.pali: Manasā kho paneva dhammaṁ viññāya amanāpaṁ na maṅku hoti appatiṭṭhitacitto adīnamānaso abyāpannacetaso.
verses.english: But if they know a disagreeable idea they’re undismayed, with mind unirritated, spirit undaunted, and heart unangered.

verses.pali: Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ajjhattaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ.
verses.english: Their mind and body are steady internally, well settled and well freed.

verses.pali: Yato kho, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā manāpāmanāpesu rūpesu ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ajjhattaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ.
verses.english: When a mendicant’s mind and body are steady internally, they’re well settled and well freed when it comes to both agreeable and disagreeable sights,

verses.pali: Sotena saddaṁ sutvā …pe…
verses.english: sounds,

verses.pali: ghānena gandhaṁ ghāyitvā …pe…
verses.english: smells,

verses.pali: jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā …pe…
verses.english: tastes,

verses.pali: kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṁ phusitvā …pe…
verses.english: touches,

verses.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya manāpāmanāpesu dhammesu ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ajjhattaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ.
verses.english: and ideas.

verses.pali: Evaṁ bhāvito kho, kuṇḍaliya, indriyasaṁvaro evaṁ bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūreti.
verses.english: That’s how sense restraint is developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the three kinds of good conduct.

verses.pali: Kathaṁ bhāvitāni ca, kuṇḍaliya, tīṇi sucaritāni kathaṁ bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti?
verses.english: And how are the three kinds of good conduct developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation?

verses.pali: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: A mendicant gives up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develops good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: Evaṁ bhāvitāni kho, kuṇḍaliya, tīṇi sucaritāni evaṁ bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti.
verses.english: That’s how the three kinds of good conduct are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, kuṇḍaliya, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā kathaṁ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti?
verses.english: And how are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors?

verses.pali: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: A mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: vedanāsu …pe…
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: citte …pe…
verses.english: mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, kuṇḍaliya, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā evaṁ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti.
verses.english: That’s how the four kinds of mindfulness meditation are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors.

verses.pali: Kathaṁ bhāvitā ca, kuṇḍaliya, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṁ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrenti?
verses.english: And how are the seven awakening factors developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and freedom?

verses.pali: Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…
verses.english: A mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

verses.pali: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.
verses.english: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

verses.pali: Evaṁ bhāvitā kho, kuṇḍaliya, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṁ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṁ paripūrentī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and freedom.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, kuṇḍaliyo paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, the wanderer Kuṇḍaliya said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama.
verses.english: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evameva bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
verses.english: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

verses.pali: Esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
verses.english: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
